column1: # Game profile of Rhythm Heaven Groove (Switch, base game v0 = 1.0.0). Plays on the Mac; handheld with Boost (no TV calibration)
# Nintendo's own engine, SDK 21.4.0 (the newest so far), NVN; no packaged textures: each texture file (graph/**/*.tex, raw BC7 or linear R8 with its description in the .spr beside it)
#   is read into memory and gets a memory pool the CPU cannot access (tex_init_fill in nvn_mtl.m). Audio is the SDK's AudioRenderer (sound/sm/**/*.cwv), whose SDK 21 command list hle_audren.c reads.
# The shaders are one BNSH, shader/shader_NX.bnsh (2 vertex and 33 pixel shaders, all 2D)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# Handheld with Boost: docked means a TV to the game, which then runs a latency calibration (press A on every fourth beat) until one passes; a phone is its own screen.
#   Boost keeps the 1920x1080 draw size (handheld Normal draws 1280x720); the game takes it from the performance mode alone (hle_oe.c)
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region (the game has no virtual address memory, so the NSP script's heap check does not run)
